input.question: With China set to relax their one-child policy, what kind of effect will this have on their population, their consumption of the world's resources and their economy over the next 50 years?
input.ground_truth: China will require more energy and more resources as it grows. If it grows. There's something to be said about the psychological effects of the one-child policy. You have an entire generation of only children, who may be preconditioned to having a single child because of it.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: With China set to relax their one-child policy, what kind of effect will this have on their population, their consumption of the world's resources and their economy over the next 50 years?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine China is like a big family. Right now, this family has only let each couple have one child. But soon, they are going to let them have more children if they want.

**What will happen to the family (population)?**  
If more babies are born, the family will get bigger! So, China will have more people living there.

**What will happen to the toys and food (resources)?**  
If there are more kids and more grown-ups, they will all want to eat, play, and use things. This means they will need more food, more water, and more stuff from the whole world. Sometimes, if too many people want the same things, there might not be enough to go around.

**What will happen to the piggy bank (economy)?**  
More people can mean more workers when they grow up. This can help the country make more things and buy more stuff, which is good for the piggy bank. But when they are little, they will need more schools, more food, and more places to live. That can cost a lot of money at first.

So, if China lets families have more children, there will be more people, more use of the world’s stuff, and the country’s money situation will change in different ways over 50 years. It could be good and also a little tricky!
